name: Great Circle (Eagle Mound centre)
source: OSM node 'Eagle Mound'; Romain & Burks lidar assessment; Wikipedia Great Circle Earthworks
notes: Ring unmistakable in DEM on 2026-10-13 render. Walls 7-9 ft with interior ditch 5-7 ft (Romain & Burks). Eagle Mound at centre, small.

name: Great Circle wall (east)
notes: Point on the ring wall; use for wall-texture queries. Gateway is on the east side, so the wall here is near the entrance.

name: Great Circle wall (west)
notes: Point on the western arc of the ring wall.

name: Octagon / Observatory Circle junction
source: OSM node 'Octagon Earthworks'; Hopewell Ceremonial Earthworks (Wikipedia); Romain & Burks
notes: Both enclosures fully visible in DEM. Golf course features (greens, bunkers) overprint the interior; country club left 2025-01-01.

name: Observatory Mound
feature_type: elongated platform mound on circle wall
notes: Clear in DEM: oblong mound astride the SW wall of the Observatory Circle.

name: Wright Earthworks surviving wall
notes: Only a short L-shaped wall segment survives in a small park at James St / Waldo St. Low relief; good hard case.

name: Alligator Effigy Mound
notes: Effigy outline visible on the headland summit in local relief. Private land with public access.

name: Dixon Mound
source: NRHP listing (Wikipedia); Homer Public Library geocode shifted ~220 ft SE to the mound seen in the DEM
notes: Library geocode is 40.2519114,-82.5250555; the mound is the bright circular blob just SE of it. Coordinates here are the DEM-observed mound centre (approx).

name: Flint Ridge quarry pit field
feature_type: field of quarry pits and spoil
source: NRHP listing / Flint Ridge State Memorial (Wikipedia)
notes: Dense pitted texture across the ridge top in the DEM. A different feature class from mounds and walls: negative-relief texture.

name: Great Hopewell Road (Van Voorhis walls area)
source: RESIDUALS tile_county.py KNOWN_SITES; Lepper; Wikipedia Great Hopewell Road
notes: The 2026-10-13 render shows an oval track-like feature at this point rather than clear parallel walls. RESIDUALS results/hopewell_trace/road_centerline.geojson (9,786 points, mean confidence 0.50) is a detection, not ground truth.

name: Infirmary Mound
source: Licking Park District / Village of Granville history page; OSM park centroid
notes: Coordinates are the park centroid (4351 Lancaster Rd). Mound not located in a 5000 ft DEM window; needs a field or park-district coordinate.

name: Salt Run Park small mound
notes: Granville village lists a small mound in Salt Run Park. No coordinates found.

name: Etna Township Mound I
source: NRHP 75001457 (address restricted); Archaeological Conservancy donation page
notes: Well preserved, wooded lot above an intermittent stream, east of Reynoldsburg near I-70. Mound II destroyed by a subdivision.

name: McDaniel Mound
source: NRHP listing (address restricted; Washington Twp near Utica)

name: Melick Mound
source: NRHP listing (south of North Fork Licking River near Utica)

name: Salisbury Hill Fort 1 (33Li7)
notes: Described 1862 as nearly obliterated; Romain & Burks saw ditch/embankment remnants in lidar on a hill above Newark. Exact hill not identified.

name: Cherry Valley Ellipse (destroyed)
feature_type: large oval enclosure with burial mounds
source: Wikipedia Newark Earthworks; hmdb marker 206092 (Hebron Rd)
notes: Destroyed by 19th-century railroad and industry. A good negative control once its footprint is georeferenced from the Salisbury 1862 map.
